clue.text: Italian water formulated as "ointment"

parts.note: the Po is Italy's longest river
something formulated has been made or put together

explanation.surface: A bottle of Italian mineral water being passed off as a skin cream.
explanation.definitionFit: A pomade is a scented greasy dressing for the hair, a kind of unguent.

clue.text: Pointed piece of rock left in boat

indicators.note: the word in tells us the letter for left sits inside the word for the boat

parts.note: a pinnace is a small boat carried by a larger ship

explanation.surface: A sharp shard of stone has been forgotten in the bottom of a boat.
explanation.walkthrough: PINNACE is a ship's tender; put L inside it, between the N and the A, to get the spire of rock.
explanation.definitionFit: A pinnacle is a tall slender peak or spire of stone.

clue.text: Horse without tail is wreck

indicators.note: a word without its tail loses its final letter, here the last letter of the word for horse

parts.note: a mare is a female horse

explanation.surface: A horse has lost its tail and is in a terrible state.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without tail' drops the E from MARE. 'wreck' is a verb here, not the noun the surface suggests.
explanation.definitionFit: To mar something is to spoil or damage it, as a scratch spoils a finish.

clue.text: Hide awful smell breaking out

indicators.note: awful suggests the letters of hide are in a terrible mess and must be rearranged

parts.note: a scent is a smell

explanation.surface: Someone hides from a dreadful stink that has suddenly appeared.
explanation.walkthrough: 'awful' is the anagram signal on 'Hide'. 'breaking out' is a botanical term for seed pods splitting open, not an escape or a rash.
explanation.definitionFit: In botany a dehiscent seed pod or anther splits open to release its contents, so it is bursting open.

clue.text: At home with exceptionally rare holy books viewed as infallible

parts.note: to be in is to be at home

indicators.note: exceptionally hints that the letters of rare are arranged out of their normal order

parts.note: NT, the New Testament, is a collection of holy books

explanation.surface: Someone at home with some rare scriptures that are regarded as never wrong.
explanation.walkthrough: 'exceptionally' is the anagram signal: RARE becomes ERRA. 'with' and 'viewed as' are links.
explanation.definitionFit: Something inerrant contains no errors at all, so it cannot be mistaken.

clue.text: Talk about one being smarter

indicators.note: about means the word for talk goes round the letter for one

parts.note: to natter is to chat or talk idly
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A conversation about which person is cleverer.
explanation.walkthrough: I goes inside NATTER, after the double T. 'smarter' means better dressed here, not cleverer.
explanation.definitionFit: Natty means neatly and fashionably dressed, so nattier is more stylish.

clue.text: Sailors crossing tree-lined road to get a bird

indicators.note: the sailors are spread across the road, so the road sits inside the letters for sailors

parts.note: RN, the Royal Navy, stands for sailors
AVE is short for avenue, a road typically lined with trees

explanation.surface: Seamen walk across a leafy avenue to go birdwatching.
explanation.walkthrough: AVE goes between R and N.
explanation.definitionFit: The raven is a large black member of the crow family.

clue.text: Star out last — this cloud has dispersed

indicators.note: dispersed means scattered, so the letters of the three words are scattered and regrouped

explanation.surface: The last star has gone out because a cloud has spread over the sky.
explanation.walkthrough: All eleven letters of STAR OUT LAST rearrange into the cloud's name.
explanation.definitionFit: Altostratus is a grey sheet of mid-level cloud that often veils the sun or a star.

clue.text: Disturbance with the French entering Spanish city

indicators.note: entering means the French article goes into the word for disturbance

parts.note: a to-do is a commotion or fuss
le is French for the

explanation.surface: Trouble breaks out when French visitors arrive in a city in Spain.
explanation.walkthrough: 'entering' is the container signal: the two-letter French article goes inside the word for a fuss, after its first two letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Toledo is a historic city in central Spain, famed for its swords.

clue.text: The absolute minimum wage?

parts.note: very poor pay is called '...', so a single nut is the smallest possible wage

explanation.definitionFit: Being paid peanuts means earning very little, so one nut is the tiniest unit of such pay.

clue.text: Direction given by PM leading silly wets

indicators.note: leading means the prime minister's name comes in front of the other part

parts.note: Lord North was British Prime Minister from 1770 to 1782

indicators.note: silly suggests the letters of wets are arranged foolishly and need sorting

explanation.surface: A Prime Minister gives orders to a group of feeble politicians.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Wets' was the nickname for moderate Tories under Thatcher, which the surface plays on. 'silly' is the anagram signal on 'wets', and 'leading' puts the PM's name first.
explanation.definitionFit: Northwest is a compass point, halfway between north and west.

clue.text: Crucial time when small medicine bottle comes round

indicators.note: comes round means the word for the bottle goes around the letter for time

parts.note: a vial is a small glass bottle for medicine

explanation.surface: It is a critical moment when a little phial of medicine is handed round.
explanation.walkthrough: T goes inside VIAL, between I and A.
explanation.definitionFit: Something vital is essential or of the greatest importance.

clue.text: Mechanic in need of some part is angry

indicators.note: some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A mechanic short of a spare part is furious.
explanation.walkthrough: The draft took 'Mechanic in need' as the definition, but 'in need of' is a link; the definition is 'Mechanic' alone, the old sense of a manual worker, as in Shakespeare's 'rude mechanicals'.
explanation.definitionFit: A mechanic in the old sense is a skilled manual worker, a craftsman.

clue.text: Lean on stick before a dance — object if the caller's incompetent?

indicators.note: in a down clue on means one part is placed above, so before, the next
before means the stick part comes ahead of the next pieces

parts.note: lean means thin
to gum is to stick
a jig is a lively dance

explanation.surface: Lean on a walking stick before taking part in a square dance with a hopeless caller.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface points to a square-dance caller; the definition means someone calling an object by name who cannot think of the word.
explanation.definitionFit: A thingumajig is a placeholder word for something whose name the speaker cannot remember.

clue.text: Charged when lacking neutrality in science

definitions.meaning: in chemistry and physics a particle that is not neutral carries a charge

explanation.walkthrough: Both halves describe the same thing, one plainly and one in scientific terms; 'when' links them.
explanation.definitionFit: Atoms carrying an electric charge have gained or lost electrons, so in physics or chemistry they are no longer neutral.

clue.text: Irish with secret cunningly hiding in shelter somewhere in the Midlands

indicators.note: hiding in means the jumbled letters are concealed inside the word for shelter

parts.note: lee is the sheltered side, away from the wind

indicators.note: cunningly suggests the letters of Irish and secret are slyly rearranged

explanation.surface: An Irishman with a secret lies low in a refuge in central England.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cunningly' is the anagram signal on IRISH SECRET, and 'hiding in' puts the jumble inside the word for shelter, between its second and third letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Leicestershire is a county in the East Midlands of England.

clue.text: One may pull locks apart

parts.note: reads like a burglar forcing doors, but the locks are tresses of hair being separated

explanation.definitionFit: A brush for the hair draws through tresses and separates tangled strands.

clue.text: Emergency over the hill? That must be communicated

parts.note: a mess is a crisis or awkward predicament
someone over the hill is old, so aged

explanation.surface: A crisis for an elderly person needs to be passed on.
explanation.walkthrough: 'That must be' is a link to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: To have messaged someone is to have sent them a text or note.

clue.text: I crash and hit gate — drunken author

indicators.note: drunken suggests the letters stagger about and must be put back in order

parts.note: the fodder, as the setter meant it with an extra A

explanation.surface: A drunk driver confesses to crashing and smashing through a gate.
explanation.walkthrough: 'drunken' rearranges the letters into the novelist's name, but as printed I CRASH HIT GATE ('and' as a link) has one A fewer than the answer, so the setter seems to have slipped.
explanation.definitionFit: Agatha Christie was the English writer of detective novels featuring Poirot and Miss Marple.

clue.text: A type upset about work, she having a deadly job

indicators.note: about means the turned word goes round the word for work
upset in a down clue turns the word for type upside down, so it reads from bottom to top

parts.note: a sort is a type or kind
OP, short for opus, is a work

explanation.surface: A certain kind of person is upset by their job, which involves killing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upset' turns SORT upside down to give TROS, and 'about' wraps that round the work. In Greek myth Atropos is the Fate who cuts the thread of life.
explanation.definitionFit: Atropos is the Fate of Greek myth who severs each mortal's thread of life, ending it.

clue.text: Jean's place in Essex

definitions.meaning: Jean ... was the 1930s Hollywood actress, so 'Jean's' surname is meant
A new town in Essex, a county north-east of London

explanation.walkthrough: Read the clue as 'Jean is place in Essex': the actress's surname and the town share the name.
explanation.definitionFit: Harlow is both the surname of the film star Jean Harlow and an Essex town built after the Second World War.

clue.text: Yours truly hospitalised and given thermal treatment

annotationWithheld.why: Yours truly hospitalised and given thermal treatment: the only parse is ME inside WARD, with 'hospitalised' both supplying WARD and signalling the insertion, one word doing two jobs
annotationWithheld.clue: Yours truly hospitalised and given thermal treatment

clue.text: One may inform you of current measure

definitions.text: One may inform you of current measure

parts.words: One may inform you of current measure
parts.note: reads as someone telling you the latest policy, but the current is electric and the device measures it

explanation.definitionFit: An electrical meter of this kind measures the strength of a current in amperes.

clue.text: Therefore under pile of rocks, part of body will be found

indicators.note: under in a down clue means the word for therefore sits below the pile of rocks

parts.note: a tor is a rocky outcrop on a hill, as on Dartmoor
so means therefore

explanation.surface: So a body part will be found buried under a cairn.
explanation.definitionFit: The torso is the trunk of the human body, without head or limbs.

clue.text: Hesitation about things coming in threes allegedly creating puzzles

indicators.note: about means the word for hesitation is turned round

parts.note: er is the sound of hesitation
the saying goes that you wait ages for a bus and then three come along at once

explanation.surface: Hesitating over things said to arrive in threes creates confusion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' turns ER into RE.
explanation.definitionFit: A rebus is a puzzle in which pictures or symbols represent words or syllables.

clue.text: Significant month in which little woman gets engaged

indicators.note: engaged means held inside, so the woman is enclosed by the month

parts.note: Mar is short for March
Jo March is a heroine of Little Women

explanation.surface: In a particular month a young woman becomes engaged to be married.
explanation.walkthrough: Neatly, Jo's surname in Little Women is March, the month itself. 'gets engaged' looks like a proposal but signals one piece held inside another.
explanation.definitionFit: Something major is important or considerable, the opposite of minor.

clue.text: Getting hold of copper to call on lady of easy virtue

indicators.note: on means the copper and call pieces are placed after the woman

parts.note: pro is short for prostitute
Cu is the chemical symbol for copper
to ring is to call on the phone

explanation.surface: A policeman visits a prostitute in order to obtain something.
explanation.walkthrough: 'copper' looks like a policeman, but it is the metal.
explanation.definitionFit: Procuring means obtaining or acquiring something.

clue.text: One with a certain sort of energy becoming president

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one
KE stands for kinetic energy

explanation.surface: Someone full of a particular energy rises to become head of state.
explanation.walkthrough: Ike was the nickname of Dwight D. Eisenhower, US President 1953 to 1961.
explanation.definitionFit: Ike was Eisenhower, the 34th US President.

clue.text: Party so huge getting out of control — a disgraceful environment

parts.note: a do is a party

indicators.note: out of control suggests the letters of so huge run wild and must be rearranged

explanation.surface: A big party gets wildly out of hand and ends in disgrace.
explanation.walkthrough: 'getting out of control' rearranges SO HUGE into GHOUSE.
explanation.definitionFit: To be 'in the doghouse' is the idiom for being out of favour after behaving badly.

clue.text: What some following story can lose — in the unfinished book, say

definitions.text: What some following story can lose

indicators.note: unfinished means the word the loses its final letter

parts.note: a book is an example of a read, as in 'a good read'

explanation.surface: A reader gets lost halfway through a book they have not finished.
explanation.walkthrough: 'unfinished' takes the last letter off the clue word 'the'. The definition refers to losing the thread of a story, a book being 'a read'.
explanation.definitionFit: To lose the thread is to lose track of a narrative's line of argument.
